title: Rollout Ops Garden — lab notes & patchwork protocol (WIP)
body:
Purpose
Quick, messy lab notes capturing an alternative mental model for cross-functional canary + A/B orchestration. Intended as a riff (garden metaphor) to help teams think about ‘planting’ exposure, watering signals, trimming bad branches, and rotating cultivars (model variants).

High level intent
- Make canaries composable: small, observable slices you can chain.
- Explicit safety gates that are cheap to evaluate (synthetic probes + real-signal heuristics).
- Fast rollback and automated fallback to a safe variant.
- Lightweight experiment artifacts so PM/DS/Eng/Ops can read a single page and act.

Garden concepts (vocabulary)
- Patch: a single change/feature (model + prompt change + config).
- Bed: traffic cohort (e.g., 0.5% global traffic, mobile EU, internal beta).
- Cultivar: model variant (quantized v2, 8-bit, opt-tune-2025).
- Watering schedule: cadence of exposure increase and synthetic probe runs.
- Pest signals: hallucination spikes, toxicity flags, regression in intent recall.

Stages (pattern)
1) Seed (local + staging): unit tests, offline evals, small synthetic harness.
2) Sprout (internal dogfood): 0.1% internal traffic + scripted probes; manual eyeballs.
3) Bed test (limited cohort): 0.5%–2% external cohort; automated telemetry gating.
4) Rapids (ramp): 2% -> 10% -> 50% with pauses and quality checks.
5) Meadow (full): 100% traffic or designated production split.

Signals to watch (fast, medium, slow)
- Fast (seconds–minutes): 5xx error rate, request queue length, p99 latency, token generation stalls, OOM/fatal VM events. Threshold examples: p99 latency > 1.5x baseline => pause ramp.
- Medium (minutes–hours): hallucination proxy (LM-qa mismatch rate), safety classifier spike (toxicity), server-side truncations, early stop rate. Threshold: hallucination-proxy increase > 3 sigma over 24h baseline.
- Slow (hours–days): user retention lift/drop, downstream rerank deterioration, model quality metrics on holdout prompts.

Example gating matrix (sketch)
- At 0.5% bed: require fast signals within baseline +/-10%, no medium signals above threshold for 3 checks over 2 hours.
- At 2%: require 6 hours of clean medium signals, automated evals (top-K QA pass >= 92%).
- At >10%: require SRE signoff if latency noise > 5% and Product + DS signoff for quality metrics.

Operational playbook (runbook-lite)
- Apply patch: redwoodctl rollout apply --patch=patch-id --bed=eu-mobile-0.5pct --cultivar=opt-q4
- Monitor: open telemetry dashboard (link to deck above), watch fast signals, smoke synthetic probes (login, common prompts).
- Pause: redwoodctl rollout pause --id=rollout-123
- Rollback: redwoodctl rollout revert --to=stable-20250201 --notify=oncall@redwood.com
- Emergency fallback: traffic-split policy auto-route to fallback model variant after 3 consecutive fail checks.

Roles & responsibilities (cross-functional)
- Product: hypothesis, success metrics, user-facing risk tolerance.
- Data Science: evaluation suite updates, hallucination proxy calibration, slice definitions.
- SRE/Infra: autoscaling parameters, latency SLO enforcement, error budget impacts.
- Developer / Serving Runtime: build/validate cultivar permutations and quant profiles.
- Legal/Security (as needed): data residency, compliance signoff for private deployments.

Experiment design checklist (short)
- Hypothesis: single sentence.
- Primary metric: name + owner + alert thresholds.
- Cost metric: expected tokens/sec cost delta.
- Safety probes: 10 most-likely fail prompts + checkers.
- Traffic slices: explicit bed names and size.
- Rollout schedule: timeline with pause windows.
- Cancel criteria: clear numeric thresholds.

Instrumentation checklist
- Ensure token-level billing tags are set per request.
- Annotate experiment requests with experiment_id, bed, cultivar in headers.
- Synthetic probe harness runs every 5m for fast signals.
- Daily batch evaluation against curated prompt set.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to compute a single composite "health score" that meaningfully combines latency, hallucination proxy, and safety classifier? (DS to prototype)
- Should we expose a single boolean "canary-safe" flag for automated ramp decisions or keep gates composable? pros/cons.
- Decide on default bed sizes for PLG customers vs. enterprise; enterprise often needs smaller micro-beds by region.
- Tie experiment metadata to billing for per-experiment cost reports (Finance ask).

Lightweight templates (for quick copy)
- One-line hypothesis: "Switch to cultivar 'opt-q4' for shorter prefix latency, expect median latency down 12% with <=1% quality loss on top-K QA."
- Rollout plan (compact): "0.5% internal 6h -> 2% public 12h -> 10% public 24h (pause checks) -> 100% if green; auto-revert on medium-signal violation."

Failure modes we saw in prior experiments (notes)
- Quiet drift: token-level cost falls but user satisfaction drops after 48h due to subtle semantic shift. Hard to detect with fast signals.
- Latency thundering herd when KV cache cold across many pods on canary pop. Mitigation: deliberate warmup traffic and staggered restart windows.
- A/B contamination: routing sticky cookies not respected across mobile webview leading to cross-contamination. Patch: add server-side sticky assignment as source of truth.

Comms & oncall cadence
- Rapid channel: #rollouts-live for immediate infra alerts.
- Decision window: notify product/DS/SRE within 15m of pause.
- Postmortem: if rollback occurs, 72h write-up with timeline, root cause, prioritized fixes.

Notes to self (unpolished)
- Need a tiny UI for 'garden view' showing beds and cultivar health at a glance. Mock: left column beds, middle: cultivar thumbnails, right: health timeline.
- Consider synthetic probe that checks for hallucination by comparing model answer to a retrieval+verified-fact pipeline. Cheap and often catches regressions.
- Prototype composite health score as weighted percentile aggregator rather than z-score average. Try weights: latency 0.25, errors 0.25, hallucination 0.35, safety 0.15.

References / anchors
- TODO: link the canonical experiment contract template from product docs (confluence id above).
- See Jira: PROD-1892 (rollout infra work), PROD-2040 (synthetic probe infra), DS-768 (hallucination proxy research).

If you read this and want to riff, add notes below or ping me in slack. This is intentionally loose — the goal is a set of pragmatic patterns teams can adopt quickly.
